strings.d1.s0.name: Fisherman's Bastion
strings.d1.s0.tips: Fairy-tale turrets and views over Parliament. The lower terraces are free; the upper tower costs 1,500 HUF (free before 08:00).
strings.d1.s1.name: Matthias Church
strings.d1.s1.tips: Colourful Zsolnay tiled roof. A coronation church with a mosaic interior.
strings.d1.s2.name: Buda Castle & Castle Hill Yürüyüşü
strings.d1.s2.tips: Palace courtyards and the Turul bird statue. The Hungarian National Gallery (4,400 HUF) is optional.
strings.d1.s3.name: Ruszwurm Cukrászda
strings.d1.s3.tips: The oldest pastry shop in the city (since 1827). Try the krémes (cream pastry); there are only 5 tables. Afterwards, take the funicular and walk across the Chain Bridge to Pest.
strings.d1.s4.name: Gerlóczy Kávéház
strings.d1.s4.tips: A Parisian-style café in Belváros, serving goulash and paprikás.
strings.d1.b0.name: Halászbástya Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: Set inside Fisherman's Bastion with views, but expensive.
strings.d1.b1.name: Hospital in the Rock
strings.d1.b1.tips: A WWII hospital and nuclear bunker beneath the castle. Visits are by guided tour only.
strings.d2.s0.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 45-minute tour (including the Holy Crown). Book tickets online days ahead and don't forget your passport.
strings.d2.s1.name: St. Stephen's Basilica
strings.d2.s1.tips: Home to the mummified right hand of St Stephen. The dome panorama costs 3,000 HUF.
strings.d2.s2.name: Belvárosi Disznótoros
strings.d2.s2.tips: Hungarian butcher's food sold by weight: hurka (rice or liver sausage), kolbász (sausage), eaten standing up.
strings.d2.s3.name: Heroes' Square
strings.d2.s3.tips: Take Metro 1, the oldest metro on the continent. See the Millennium Monument and the seven tribal chieftains.
strings.d2.s4.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
strings.d2.s4.tips: Europe's largest thermal bath, in a yellow palace with a 38°C outdoor pool and chess tables. Bring your own slippers and towel; it's cheaper on weekdays.
strings.d2.b0.name: Gellért Thermal Bath
strings.d2.b0.tips: An Art Nouveau bath, as an alternative to Széchenyi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Vajdahunyad Vár Restoranı Városliget
strings.d2.b1.tips: A restaurant in the castle park.
strings.d3.s0.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
strings.d3.s0.tips: The largest synagogue in Europe, with the Weeping Willow memorial. Closed on Saturdays.
strings.d3.s1.name: Karaván Street Food
strings.d3.s1.tips: A food-truck courtyard next to Szimpla. Try lángos (fried dough with garlic and cheese) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake).
strings.d3.s2.name: Great Market Hall
strings.d3.s2.tips: An iron-framed market hall from 1897. Look for paprika and salami, with lángos on the upper floor. Closed on Sundays.
strings.d3.s3.name: Liberty Bridge & Gellért Hill
strings.d3.s3.tips: The green bridge, then a 30-minute climb up Gellért Hill for a Citadella panorama at sunset.
strings.d3.s4.name: Szimpla Kert
strings.d3.s4.tips: The original ruin bar (2002), with a bicycle café and a plant garden. Entry is free and a beer costs 1,000 HUF.
strings.d3.b0.name: Mazel Tov
strings.d3.b0.tips: A Middle Eastern garden restaurant in the Jewish Quarter. Book ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Hungarian National Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: The steps where the 1848 revolution unfolded; an alternative to the market.
strings.d4.s0.name: Szentendre Fő tér
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take the HÉV train (40 minutes from Batthyány tér) to a Baroque artists' town with Serbian churches.
strings.d4.s1.name: Blagoveštenska Church Szentendre
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Serbian Orthodox church on the square.
strings.d4.s2.name: Aranysárkány Vendéglő
strings.d4.s2.tips: The town's classic restaurant, serving goulash and paprikás csirke (paprika chicken).
strings.d4.s3.name: Szentendre Tuna Kıyısı
strings.d4.s3.tips: A riverside walk. In summer you can return by boat (Mahart), taking 1.5 hours.
strings.d4.s4.name: Skanzen Open Air Museum
strings.d4.s4.tips: A museum of Hungarian village houses, 10 minutes by bus (April to October).
strings.d4.b0.name: Álom Lángos Szentendre
strings.d4.b0.tips: The town's famous lángos, from a small stand.
strings.d4.b1.name: Visegrád Castle
strings.d4.b1.tips: A castle on the Danube Bend, reached by bus; an alternative to Skanzen.
strings.d5.s0.name: Margaret Island
strings.d5.s0.tips: A park island in the Danube. Rent a bike or pedal cart, and see the musical fountain, Japanese garden and ruins.
strings.d5.s1.name: Andrássy Avenue
strings.d5.s1.tips: A UNESCO-listed boulevard with the Opera, Liszt Square and luxury shops.
strings.d5.s2.name: Menza Liszt Ferenc tér
strings.d5.s2.tips: A retro Hungarian restaurant on Liszt Square. Try the goulash.
strings.d5.s3.name: House of Terror
strings.d5.s3.tips: The former Nazi and communist secret police headquarters. Heavy going but important. Closed on Mondays.
strings.d5.s4.name: Hungarian State Opera
strings.d5.s4.tips: A tour of the neo-Renaissance opera house (in English at 13:30 and 15:00), or evening tickets from 5,000 HUF.
strings.d5.b0.name: New York Café
strings.d5.b0.tips: Billed as 'the most beautiful café in the world'. Expect queues and high prices; an alternative to Menza.
strings.d5.b1.name: Miniversum
strings.d5.b1.tips: Miniature Hungarian model trains; an alternative to the House of Terror (with children).
strings.d6.s0.name: Aquincum Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: Ruins of a Roman city in Óbuda, reached by HÉV.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lukács Thermal Bath
strings.d6.s1.tips: The locals' bath, quieter and cheaper than Széchenyi.
strings.d6.s2.name: Bambi Eszpresszó
strings.d6.s2.tips: A communist-era café unchanged since 1961, in Buda.
strings.d6.s3.name: Batthyány tér Parlamento Manzarası
strings.d6.s3.tips: The best view of Parliament, from across the river.
strings.d6.s4.name: Danube Sightseeing Cruise
strings.d6.s4.tips: A one-hour evening boat trip with the lights on. Parliament and the Castle glow like gold.
strings.d6.b0.name: Pesti Disznó
strings.d6.b0.tips: Modern Hungarian cooking with plenty of pork, in Pest.
strings.d6.b1.name: Óbuda Fő tér
strings.d6.b1.tips: Old Óbuda's square, with its statues of figures under umbrellas; an alternative to Aquincum.
strings.d7.s0.name: Váci Street
strings.d7.s0.tips: A pedestrian shopping street. Pick up paprika and Tokaji wine as souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Vörösmarty Square Gerbeaud
strings.d7.s1.tips: A pastry shop from 1858. Have Dobos torta and coffee as your farewell.
strings.d7.s2.name: Danube Promenade Little Princess
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Little Princess statue, and tram line 2 running along the riverbank.
strings.d7.s3.name: Deák Ferenc tér 100E Havalimanı Otobüsü
strings.d7.s3.tips: The direct 100E bus takes 40 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Café Central Budapest
strings.d7.b0.tips: A literary café from 1887; an alternative to Gerbeaud.
strings.d7.b1.name: Erzsébet tér Ferris Wheel
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Budapest Eye Ferris wheel; an alternative to the river.
strings.note0: A Budapest Card or 24-hour ticket costs about 2,500 HUF. Tram 2 has views of both riverbanks. The 100E airport bus costs 2,200 HUF. Metro 1 is a historic line.
strings.note1: Summer temperatures are 28-32°C. The Sziget Festival is held in August (on an island in Óbuda). The baths' outdoor pools are a good option, boat evenings are cool, and there are fireworks on 20 August.
strings.note2: Baths cost 12-15,000 HUF (cheaper on weekdays), Parliament 10,000 and the synagogue 12,000. Renting towels and slippers is expensive, so bring your own.
strings.note3: Goulash (it's a soup!), pörkölt (stew), lángos, kürtőskalács, Dobos torta. Tip 10-12%, but check whether a 'szervizdíj' (service charge) has already been added to the bill.
strings.note4: Pay in cash in forints. Places that accept EUR give poor rates. Beware the 'no commission' trap at exchange offices, and at ATMs choose your own bank's rate.
strings.note5: The ruin pubs are around Kazinczy Street. The synagogue is closed on Saturdays and the Great Market Hall on Sundays.
